add.text: An obvious cause for the jaundice has been identified
add.notes: US Abdomen p30 Acute 48 h: 'Painless jaundice without obvious cause'. true = an obvious cause is apparent; the criterion needs false. Clinical judgement - proposed AD-17 attestation candidate (not added to attestationIndicators: no attestationWording drafted). See sites/us-abdomen-adult REVIEW Q2.

add.text: GGT raised (higher than the upper limit of normal)
add.notes: Boolean flag (KI-06). US Abdomen p30 'GGT higher than the ULN' / 'raised ALP and GGT'; p32-33 'raised GGT', 'normal GGT'.

add.text: GGT as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory
add.notes: KI-13, same pattern as lab.alp.timesULN. US Abdomen p32 'Isolated raised GGT more than 5 times the ULN' (P3) and 'less than 5 times the ULN' (alternative management).

add.text: GGT remains higher than the upper limit of normal on repeat testing
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Repeat GGT remains higher than the ULN'. The repeat-test counterpart of lab.ggt.raised.

add.text: GGT on repeat testing as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3: 'Isolated raised GGT more than 5 times the ULN and persists on re-testing after 3 months' (REVIEW Q11 reads 'persists' as still above 5 x ULN).

add.text: ALP remains higher than the upper limit of normal on repeat testing
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Repeat ALP remains higher than the ULN'. Named after the published lab.alp.high (REVIEW Q15 of the vocabulary notes).

add.text: Liver blood tests have been repeated 3 months or more after the initial presentation
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 'repeat testing 3 months or more after the initial presentation'; p32 're-testing after 3 months'. Not lab.repeatConfirmed, whose text fixes a three-week interval and a persistence judgement across several analytes.

add.text: The raised liver blood test result is isolated (the other liver blood tests are normal)
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 'Isolated raised GGT'; p33 'Isolated raised bilirubin'. One concept for both (KI-01).

add.text: Bilirubin raised
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 'Isolated raised bilirubin'. P2 bullet 2's '+/- bilirubin' is modifier wording (KI-05) and does not use it.

add.text: ALT value (IU/L)
add.notes: KI-06/KI-13: a .value sibling exists because the criterion states a numeric threshold: US Abdomen p31 'ALT greater than 120 IU/L'.

add.text: Suspected acute biliary colic or cholecystitis
add.notes: US Abdomen p30 P2 'Suspected acute cholecystitis / biliary colic ... where symptoms settle with analgesia'; p31 P3 'Suspected resolved acute biliary colic or cholecystitis'. Distinct from redflag.cholecystitisOrCholangitis (intractable, not relieved by simple analgesia).

add.text: Symptoms settle with analgesia
add.notes: US Abdomen p30 P2: 'where symptoms settle with analgesia'.

add.text: The suspected acute biliary colic or cholecystitis has resolved
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Suspected resolved acute biliary colic or cholecystitis'.

add.text: Recurrent right upper quadrant or epigastric pain
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Recurrent right upper quadrant / epigastric, non-dyspepsia pain'. 'non-dyspepsia' is symptom.dyspepsia = false.

add.text: Dyspepsia
add.notes: One concept, two roles (KI-01): negated in US Abdomen p31 P3 ('non-dyspepsia pain') and a redirect at p33 ('Dyspepsia – See local HealthPathway').

add.text: Newly suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3: 'Asymptomatic, newly suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm'. Distinct from redflag.rupturedAAA and from known AAA under surveillance (advice.aaaSurveillance).

add.text: The suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm is asymptomatic
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3: 'Asymptomatic, newly suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm'.

add.text: Non-pulsatile abdominal mass
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 'Non-pulsatile abdominal mass and suspected enlarged liver on examination' and alternative management 'Upper abdominal non-pulsatile mass, not consistent with hepatomegaly'.

add.text: The abdominal mass is in the upper abdomen
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 alternative management: 'Upper abdominal non-pulsatile mass'.

add.text: Suspected enlarged liver on examination
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 'suspected enlarged liver on examination'; answered false for the alternative-management item 'not consistent with hepatomegaly'.

add.text: Suspected colorectal neoplasm
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management (Colorectal Symptoms HealthPathway).

add.text: New unilateral lymphoedema
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management.

add.text: Suspected or symptomatic chronic pancreatitis
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management ('request acute general surgery assessment'). Not a national red flag: it is printed in the alternative-management row.

add.text: Urinary tract presentations and suspected renal abnormality
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management, published wording kept as one indicator (see sites/us-abdomen-adult REVIEW Q21). US Renal may hold the underlying concepts.

add.text: Isolated bloating
add.notes: US Abdomen p33: alternative management ('Isolated bloating with associated clinical symptoms') and not routinely funded ('Isolated bloating with no other features of concern'); the two differ only in workup.clinicalFeaturesOfConcern.

add.text: The presenting problem has previously been imaged
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'non-dyspepsia pain without previous imaging' - no modality or region is printed (REVIEW Q6). Breaks the imaging.<examSlug>.<window> shape because the source names no exam.

add.text: Previous imaging has shown gallstones
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'without previous imaging which showed gallstones'.

add.text: The patient is a potential candidate for and would accept a cholecystectomy
add.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3. Clinical judgement plus patient preference - proposed AD-17 attestation candidate.

add.text: Conservative methods (e.g. weight loss and lifestyle alterations or medication change) have been unsuccessful
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 (ALT bullet). The 'e.g.' list is illustrative (KI-05).

add.text: Clinical features of concern are present
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 'No clinical features of concern' (answered false); p33 bloating items ('with associated clinical symptoms' / 'with no other features of concern'), REVIEW Q20. Clinical judgement - proposed AD-17 attestation candidate.

add.text: Suspicion of underlying malignancy
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 alternative management. Not workup.strongSuspicionMalignancy: the source says 'suspicion', not 'strong suspicion' (REVIEW Q19). Vocabulary owner to rule whether this is a near-duplicate (KI-01). Proposed AD-17 attestation candidate.

add.text: High risk factors present (diabetes, obesity, medications that affect the liver, e.g. statins)
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 (ALT bullet): 'in patients with high risk factors (diabetes, obesity, medications that affect the liver, e.g. statins)'. One indicator for the printed group (REVIEW Q9). The `patient` group description says demographics; there is no history group.

add.text: HCC surveillance using liver ultrasound has been recommended by a gastroenterologist or other secondary care specialist, as part of long-term monitoring by Hepatitis Foundation of NZ, or by an agreed local pathway
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 S3 bullet 1, one indicator for the bullet.

add.text: Surveillance of a known abdominal aortic aneurysm is due according to local HealthPathway, New Zealand Vascular Society guidelines or secondary care specialist advice
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 S3 bullet 2, one indicator for the bullet.

add.text: Follow up of an incidental finding on imaging (including gallbladder polyps) is due according to the Incidental Findings on Imaging HealthPathway or radiology report advice
add.notes: US Abdomen p32 S3 bullet 3, one indicator for the bullet. Other sites with incidental-finding follow-up rows may share it.

add.text: Hernia in adults
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded. Read as the reason for the request (REVIEW Q18).

add.text: Infective hepatitis
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded. Read as the reason for the request (REVIEW Q18); interacts with S3 HCC surveillance under Hepatitis Foundation monitoring.

add.text: Follow-up imaging of previously diagnosed gallstones in asymptomatic patients
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded. A scenario marker (the purpose of the request), not imaging.gallstones.ever + asymptomatic.

add.text: Follow up imaging of simple renal or hepatic cysts
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded.

add.text: Screening for aortic aneurysm
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded ('Screening for: aortic aneurysm').

add.text: Screening for fatty liver
add.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded ('Screening for: fatty liver').
